messages:
Priya Nair: Hey team — we just switched our embeddings calls to use the int8 quantization profile and now our similarity pipeline is exploding. Downstream join fails with a dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 384. We didn’t change any code besides setting quantization=\"int8\". Anyone seen this?

Alex Gomez: Hi Priya — sorry you're hitting this. Quick Qs: which model name/version are you calling? Can you paste the raw response (or a redacted snippet) from the /embeddings endpoint? Also what SDK/HTTP client are you using and are you batching multiple inputs per request?

Priya Nair: Model is \"redwood-embed-3\" (we thought the int8 profile would be the same dims). Using python sdk v0.9.2, we send a list of texts (batch size ~32). Raw error from our join job: 
```
ValueError: shapes (N,768) and (M,384) not aligned: expected axis 1 of second array to be 768
```
and a snippet from our save step shows:
```
{"id":"abc123","embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ... , 0.12] }  # length shows 384 when we inspect
```

Samir Patel: Important note — quantization (fp16/int8) should not change a model's output dimensionality. If you actually got 384 values, either: 1) you hit a different model variant (e.g., a "-small" or "reduced-dim" variant), 2) post-processing (PCA/LSH) was accidentally enabled, or 3) client-side parsing flattened/halved values somehow.

Alex Gomez: +1. Can you run a single-request sanity check with batch_size=1 and print len(embedding) directly from the API response (not from any saved artifact)? E.g.:
```python
# repro snippet
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=...)
r = c.embeddings(model="redwood-embed-3", input=["test sentence"], quantization="int8")
print(len(r['data'][0]['embedding']))
print(r['model'])
```
Or with curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-3","input":["hello world"],"quantization":"int8"}'
```

Priya Nair: Ran that. From the raw API: len(...) -> 384. Response includes \"model\": \"redwood-embed-3@v1-int8\". So looks like the int8 variant reports as a different model ref. We must've assumed variants shared dims.

Samir Patel: That explains it. The int8 build we rolled out for some smaller-instance options is actually a compact variant that uses a reduced projection to save memory/IO; it returns 384-d vectors. That was a release decision for a specific flavor but we should never surprise users without explicit docs.

Alex Gomez: Okay — immediate steps: 1) For Priya, if you need 768 dims, switch to the full-dimension model name explicitly (e.g., `redwood-embed-3@v1-full` or set `variant":"full"` in your request). 2) We'll add an explicit field in the response (e.g., `embedding_dim`) so SDKs can validate. 3) Escalating to eng-ml to review the naming/compatibility docs and to check why the int8 variant returned with a different model token.

Priya Nair: Switching to `redwood-embed-3@v1-full` fixed it immediately — len -> 768 and joins succeed. Thanks. Any note on quality when using int8 vs fp16? We also saw cosine scores drop when comparing fp16->int8 outputs even when dims matched on other model variants.

Samir Patel: Good catch. int8 does quantize values aggressively; it can introduce small numeric shifts that matter for tight similarity thresholds, especially for older PCA'd embeddings. In general: fp16 preserves numeric range better; int8 is for throughput/cost. If you need strict semantic similarity preservation, prefer fp16 or no quantization.

Jesse Carter: For throughput concerns you mentioned, Priya — try our batching suggestions: keep batch_size around 8-32 depending on tokens, enable prefix KV caching for chat-like workloads, and use the `throughput_profile` param (if available) to bias toward throughput vs latency. But again: batching won't change dims.

Priya Nair: Thanks — that helps. For our product we need 768 dims and reasonable cost. We'll opt for fp16 and tune batch_size. Can you add a short writeup of this thread to the incident ticket so other customers don't hit surprises?

Alex Gomez: Will do. Creating ticket INC-4591 and assigning to eng-ml for docs + variant naming cleanup. I'll paste the repro steps and the exact model names. Closing loop here — let me know if you want help updating your code to pin `@v1-full` programmatically. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: Incident INC-4591 created and assigned to eng-ml. Priority: P2.

Priya Nair: Appreciate it — marking resolved for now. If we see quality regression with fp16 we'll re-open. :pray:
